text: The BS Software Engineering Suggested Four Year Plan (2023-2024 Catalog) shows a recommended course sequence; courses may be taken in any order, as long as prerequisites are met. The plan's legend distinguishes pre- or co-requisites, prerequisites, and the prerequisite critical path. Before Calculus I (MATH 2413 or MATH 2417), students need MATH 2312 with a C or better or a score of 80% on ALEKS. A grade of C- or better is needed in MATH 2413 or MATH 2417 to move forward. A grade of C or better is required for CS 1336, CS 1337, CS 2305, and CS 2336. SE 4485 Software Engineering Project is offered Fall/Spring, and the plan notes that at least two of four marked prerequisite courses must be complete to begin the project.
source_title: BS Software Engineering Suggested Four Year Plan (2023-2024 Catalog)
section_heading: Suggested Four Year Plan: Overview and Grade Requirements

text: In the BS Software Engineering Suggested Four Year Plan (2023-2024 Catalog), the freshman year includes the following. Freshman, first semester: CS 1200 Introduction to CS & SE; ECS 1100 Introduction to Engineering & CS; MATH 2413 or 2417 Calculus I; CS 1436 Programming Fundamentals; 6 hours of CORE (see core choices); and UNIV 1010 Freshman Seminar. Freshman, second semester: CS 1337 Computer Science I; CS 2305 Discrete Mathematics I; MATH 2414 or 2419 Calculus II; PHYS 2325 Mechanics and Heat; PHYS 2125 Mechanics and Heat Lab; and 3 hours of CORE. The chart also shows CS 2336 or CS 2337 as an alternative path with the note "AP score of at least 4."
source_title: BS Software Engineering Suggested Four Year Plan (2023-2024 Catalog)
section_heading: Suggested Four Year Plan: Freshman Year

text: In the BS Software Engineering Suggested Four Year Plan (2023-2024 Catalog), the sophomore year includes the following. Sophomore, first semester: SE 3306 Mathematics Foundations of SE; SE 2340 Computer Architecture; CS 2336 or CS 2337 Computer Science II; PHYS 2326 Electricity and Magnetism; and PHYS 2126 Electricity and Magnetism Lab. Sophomore, second semester: SE 3341 Probability & Statistics in CS; SE 3345 Algorithms Analysis & Data Structures; SE 3377 Systems Programming in UNIX and Other Environments; MATH 2418 Linear Algebra; and 3 hours of CORE.
source_title: BS Software Engineering Suggested Four Year Plan (2023-2024 Catalog)
section_heading: Suggested Four Year Plan: Sophomore Year

text: In the BS Software Engineering Suggested Four Year Plan (2023-2024 Catalog), the junior year includes the following. Junior, first semester: SE 3354 Software Engineering; SE 4348 Operating Systems; an SE Guided Elective (SE 43XX); ECS 3390 Professional & Technical Communication; 3 hours of CORE; and UNIV 2020 Core Curriculum Assessment. Junior, second semester: SE 4381 Software Project Planning & Management; SE 4352 Software Architecture & Design; 3 hours of SE Guided Elective (SE 43XX); SE 4347 Database Systems; and SE/CS 3162 Professional Responsibility in CS & SE.
source_title: BS Software Engineering Suggested Four Year Plan (2023-2024 Catalog)
section_heading: Suggested Four Year Plan: Junior Year

text: In the BS Software Engineering Suggested Four Year Plan (2023-2024 Catalog), the senior year includes the following. Senior, first semester: SE 4367 Software Testing, Verification, Validation, QA; SE 4351 Requirements Engineering; 3 hours of SE Guided Elective (SE/CS 43XX); 3 hours of Math Guided Elective; and 3 hours of CORE. Senior, second semester: SE 4485 Software Engineering Project (offered Fall/Spring); 3 hours of SE Guided Elective (SE 43XX); and 4 hours of Free Elective (see advisor).
source_title: BS Software Engineering Suggested Four Year Plan (2023-2024 Catalog)

text: Core choices in the BS Software Engineering Suggested Four Year Plan (2023-2024 Catalog) include: RHET 1302; GOVT 2305 and GOVT 2306; 3 hours from AMS 2300, AMS 2341, HUMA 1301, LIT 2331, PHIL 1301, or PHIL 2316, 2317; 6 hours from HIST 1301, HIST 1302, HIST 2301, HIST 2330, or HIST 2332; 3 hours from AHST 1303, 1304, 2331, ARTS 1301, DANC 1310, FILM 2332, MUSI 1306, or THEA 1310; and 3 hours from CRIM 1301, ECON 2301, ECON 2302, GEOG 2303, or PSY 2301.
